note: ep06 Short 'Walt and June' (2026-10-17), 9:16, published the same day as the long-form v2. Hook in the first line, no assumed knowledge. Every number is checked by tools/validate-ep06-story.mjs (short section) and asserted by render/short-walt-june.html. Walt and June are illustrations.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: Two people retire with *a million dollars*. Both take out forty thousand a year, plus inflation. One retires into the Great Depression. One into the calm sixties. *Who runs out?*

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: I'm Walt. Nineteen twenty-nine. Stocks crash *eighty-five percent*.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: But prices fell too. My money stretched further.

lines.speaker: J
lines.text: I'm June. Nineteen sixty-six. No crash. Just prices going up, *year after year*.

lines.speaker: J
lines.text: By nineteen eighty-two, prices had *nearly tripled*. I kept selling, just to keep up.

lines.speaker: W
lines.text: Thirty years later, I still have *seven hundred forty-nine thousand*.

lines.speaker: N
lines.text: The crash didn't sink Walt. *Rising prices* sank June. The full story, and what it means for you, is on the channel.
